1.1.2.11-f10.accuracy_reason: Seneca, Phaedra 177–179 does read 'quae memoras scio / vera esse, nutrix; sed furor cogit sequi / peiora', and the note describes Burton's changes correctly.

1.1.2.11-f5.accuracy_reason: Aeneid 5.21–22: Palinurus says this of the storm that turns the fleet towards Sicily; Burton's English does carry the sentence on.

1.1.2.11-f8.accuracy_reason: Metamorphoses 7.19–20 opens 'sed trahit invitam nova vis'; Medea speaks there, torn between love of Jason and duty to her father.

1.1.2.11-f9.accuracy_reason: Amores 2.4.5 is correct; the poem is Ovid confessing his own faults.
